description: Panel 1: COMPLETED requests in estate_web (ds_psql) where public.balance still shows token_balance ≥ 1. Panel 2: estate_ledger_adapter (ds_psql_adapter) public.wallet_tx FATAL_ERROR for TRC20/ERC20 only (test bid_id excluded)  -  bid_id, created_at, send_at (no updated_at on table; aligned with alert refId D). Typical flow for panel 1: transit_wallet, update-balances, re-check estate_web / estate_contract.

panels.description: Tracks COMPLETED requests whose balance row may be stale (token_balance ≥ 1 excludes dust). Excluded request_id: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 (TRX transit CHANGE_ME, manually acknowledged stale balance 2026-07-15). If rows appear here, check adapter transit_wallet for the address, refresh via estate-ledger-adapter update-balances when possible, then verify balances in estate_web and estate_contract.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT r.id, r.transit_wallet, b.token_balance, r.status_date
FROM public.request AS r
JOIN public.balance b ON r.id = b.request_id
WHERE r.status = 'COMPLETED' AND b.token_balance >= 1
  AND r.id NOT IN (
    '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'
  )
ORDER BY r.status_date DESC;

panels.title: COMPLETED + token_balance ≥ 1 (no dust)

panels.description: Lists wallet_tx rows with status FATAL_ERROR, tx_type TRC20_TRANSFER or ERC20_TRANSFER only. Excluded bid_id values are documented placeholders (test and resolved tickets). Columns created_at and send_at match the alert rule refId D (estate-databases-global.yaml). If rows appear, note bid_id and follow runbook: confirm single FATAL per bid, then re-queue via NEW + new id on wallet_tx if agreed with the product owner.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT bid_id, id AS wallet_tx_id, status, tx_type, created_at, send_at
FROM public.wallet_tx
WHERE status = 'FATAL_ERROR'
  AND (tx_type = 'TRC20_TRANSFER' OR tx_type = 'ERC20_TRANSFER')
  AND bid_id NOT IN (
    '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002',
    '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003',
    '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004',
    '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005',
    '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006',
    '00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000007'
  )
ORDER BY bid_id, send_at DESC NULLS LAST, created_at DESC NULLS LAST;
